subject: Control-plane egress exception request — Acme Diagnostics
messages:
From: Acme Diagnostics <infra@acme-diagnostics.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai
Cc: security@envoysec.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Control-plane egress exception request — Acme Diagnostics

Hi Ben,

We are preparing to onboard Redwood Private (on-prem runtime) in our staging cluster and need a short-lived egress exception for the control plane and model sync endpoints. Our security team requires an official request with:

- Exact destination IPs/FQDNs we should allow
- Port/protocol and SNI expectations (if any)
- Certificate validation requirements (CA / pinning guidance)
- Expected frequency and data types (TLS handshakes, model fetch, telemetry)
- Whether the control plane will accept connections from ephemeral source IPs (NAT) or requires static bindable IPs

I've attached our network diagram and the completed exception form. Can Redwood confirm the minimal firewall rules so we can submit to our Change Approval Board?

Thanks,
Marcus Lopez
Infra Engineer — Acme Diagnostics
attachment: acme-egress-exception-form.pdf (PDF)
attachment: network-diagram-acme-onprem_v2.png (PNG)

From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: Marcus Lopez <infra@acme-diagnostics.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai, security@envoysec.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control-plane egress exception request — Acme Diagnostics

Marcus — thanks for the form and diagram. Quick read-through and a few clarifying items before we hand this off to Security/Networking: 

1) Destination endpoints: we operate a small set of control-plane FQDNs (control.redwood-inference.com, artifacts.redwood-inference.com, telemetry.redwood-inference.com) and a range of egress IPs for the next 90 days. We'll provide the exact IP list below in a follow-up email (we rotate ephemeral IPs weekly, but will give a pinned list for the 90-day window).

2) Ports/Protocol: TLS 1.2+ over TCP 443 for all control and artifact traffic. If you have deep inspection that needs port ranges, only 443 is required.

3) SNI/CN expectations: SNI should be one of the control FQDNs above. We recommend validating CN/SAN on the certificate chain; if you require pinning, Redwood can provide a stable leaf-cert fingerprint for the 90-day window.

4) mTLS: Control plane auth is mutual-TLS optional for Private deployments by request. For your PCI environment we recommend enabling client certs. If you opt into mTLS, we'll coordinate cert exchange and rotation cadence.

5) Traffic profile: model fetch (occasional large TLS GETs for checkpoint sync), heartbeat/metrics (regular small POSTs), and occasional package downloads. Total throughput depends on deployment size — you listed 8 GPUs in staging; expected peak egress ~60 Mbps during syncs.

Action items (for our teams):
- Redwood to provide pinned IP list for 90 days (ben) — target EOD tomorrow.
- Kimberly to confirm whether we should supply cert fingerprint and rotation schedule.
- David to propose recommended firewall ACL snippets (CIDR, ports, SNI).

I'll loop in Kimberly and David for the technical firewall language.

—Ben

From: kimberly_park@redwood.ai
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, Marcus Lopez <infra@acme-diagnostics.com>
Cc: david_kim@redwood.ai, security@envoysec.com
Date: Mon, 18 May 2026 13:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Control-plane egress exception request — Acme Diagnostics

Marcus / Ben — short note from Security: we can approve a scoped exception provided Acme accepts the following compensating controls:

- Allowlist only the specified FQDNs and the pinned 90-day IP block we will provide. Do not allow 0.0.0.0/0 outbound to those services.
- Enforce TLS 1.2+ and reject weak ciphers.
- Require certificate validation; pin leaf cert fingerprint for the 90-day window. If Acme enables mTLS we'll require proof of key ownership and a key-rotation calendar (minimum 90-day validity per cert).
- Limit access to ports TCP/443 and drop all other outbound ports to those hosts.
- Logging: retain TLS termination logs and SNI metadata for 180 days (to satisfy audit).
- Telemetry: send a one-time evidence bundle (curl -I to each FQDN) that includes TLS chain and SNI; Redwood will verify during the kickoff call.

David — please propose the firewall ACL snippets (CIDR + port) we want them to paste into their Change Request. Marcus — if you can confirm your change window and CAB date we'll prioritize the fingerpint and IP list delivery.

-Kimberly

From: david_kim@redwood.ai
To: Marcus Lopez <infra@acme-diagnostics.com>, ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 19 May 2026 10:08:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control-plane egress exception request — Acme Diagnostics

Marcus — firewall snippet for Change Request (paste as-is):

--- start snippet ---
# Allow Redwood control plane traffic (90-day pinned IP block)
ALLOW tcp from SOURCE_NET_YOUR_HOSTS to 198.51.100.128/26 port 443 comment "Redwood control-plane egress (control.redwood-inference.com)"
ALLOW tcp from SOURCE_NET_YOUR_HOSTS to 203.0.113.0/27 port 443 comment "Redwood artifacts (artifacts.redwood-inference.com)"
ALLOW tcp from SOURCE_NET_YOUR_HOSTS to 198.51.101.0/27 port 443 comment "Redwood telemetry (telemetry.redwood-inference.com)"
# Deny all other outbound to those FQDNs/IPs by default
DENY tcp from SOURCE_NET_YOUR_HOSTS to ANY port 1-65535 comment "Default outbound deny — only explicit allows allowed"
--- end snippet ---

Notes:
- Replace SOURCE_NET_YOUR_HOSTS with your internal CIDR(s) for the on-prem runtime.
- The CIDRs above are the pinned /90-day window assignments; we'll send the authoritative list and update if NAT egress changes.
- If you enable mTLS, allow TCP 443 only and add an ingress rule on your firewall to accept (mutual) TLS flows from Redwood's client cert fingerprint.

I'll attach a short example iptables rule if you need it for host-based firewall.

-David

From: Marcus Lopez <infra@acme-diagnostics.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai, david_kim@redwood.ai
Cc: security@envoysec.com
Date: Thu, 20 May 2026 15:43:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Control-plane egress exception request — Acme Diagnostics

Thanks, everyone — CAB is scheduled for Tue 2026-05-25. We have everything needed for the packet: network diagram, change snippet, and the pinned 90-day CIDRs you provided in the snippet. A few clarifications from our CAB reviewer: 

- Can Redwood confirm the cadence of IP rotation after the 90-day pin window? We need a lifecycle plan to attach to the change.
- For telemetry logs: we will store SNI + TLS metadata for 180 days as requested. Please send the evidence bundle URL when you run the curl checks.
- On mTLS: we will enable for production only. For staging, we will proceed with one-way TLS and cert pinning as discussed.

If you can send the final fingerprint(s) and the Drive link to the evidence bundle tomorrow, we'll mark the change as "ready for CAB". Appreciate the quick turnaround.

—Marcus
